sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 17-10-2020 at about 8.30 p.m., the Petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing No.KA-01- ED-886 on Doddaballapura road when he reached near Makali, at that time a car bearing No.KA-43-8593 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the right side of the motor cycle from opposite direction.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was admitted to Doddaballapura Government hospital and thereafter shifted to ESIC, MC PGIMSR and Model hospital.
Thereafter again the petitioner was shifted to Spine Care & Ortho care hospital, wherein he is still under treatment.
He has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as driver and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed objections to the main petition.

Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further he contended that he is not liable to pay any compensation as the vehicle was insured with 2 nd respondent as on the date of accident.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further it contended that the accident was caused solely due to carelessness and negligence of the rider of the motor cycle and thereby caused the accident.

Further it contended that the driver of the vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and the owner of the car entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid driving licence.

It admitted the Raju Alias Raja vs Ravishankar B.G on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82654548/

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 17-10-2020 at about 8.30 p.m. on Gowribidanur, Doddaballapura road near Makali,
Tubagere Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA-43-8593?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.11.
Thereafter, the petitioner got examined 3 witnesses as PW.2 to P.W.4 and got marked document as per Ex.P.12 to 20 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 6 and closed its side evidence.
Respondent No.1 has not chosen to lead evidence.

8. Learned Counsel for the petitioner relied upon the following judgments:
1. Venkataramanappa VS S.Ananda & others,2013 ACJ 1581 (KANT)
2. Jakir Hussein VS Sabir and Others, 2015 ACJ 721, (SC)
3. Aabid Khan Vs Dinesh & others, 2024 AAC 1121 9.

 REASONS 11. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 17-10-2020 at about 8.30 p.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Regn.No.KA-43- 8593 by its driver.

sentences.text: 12. On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Regn.No.KA-43-8593 by its driver.
13. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-11.
He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 is the true copy of FIR along with complaint, Ex.P.2 is the true copy of statement, Ex.P.3 is the true copy of spot panchanama, Ex.P.4 is the true IMV report, Ex.P.5 is true copy of charge sheet,

Ex.P.6 is the true copy of vehicle particulars, Ex.P.7 is the true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.9 is the notarised copy of aadhar card, Ex.P.10 is the medical bills and Ex.P.11 is the prescriptions.

14. Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR along with Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Doddaballapura Police Station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the driver of car bearing Regn.No.KA-43-8593 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the spot panchanama which shows that it was made in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects and also justify the fact of involvement of vehicle in question in the accident.

The document Ex.P.5 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the Doddaballapura Police have Charge-sheeted the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.
The document Ex.P.7 is the wound certificate which shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.8 is the discharge summary.

15. Further, P.W.1 examined Medical records Technician as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 to 16 i.e.,
authorization letter, inpatient records, copy of MLC register, copy of police intimation and X-rays.
Further PW.1 got examined Dr.K.Surendra Shetty as P.W.3 and got marked Ex.P.17 to 19 i.e., case sheet, two X-rays and CD.
Further PW.1 got examined Dr.Ravikumar Bellubbi as PW.4 and got marked Ex.P.20 i.e., authorisation letter.
16. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross- examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 put a suggestion that the rider of motor cycle had informed in the ESI hospital that the petitioner was riding the bike with the influence of alcohol.
But, on perusal of entire police records no such evidence is found and respondent No.2 did not take such contention in his written statement.

Moreover the petitioner was not the rider of the bike, but he was the pillion Raju Alias Raja vs Ravishankar B.G on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82654548/
4 rider of the bike.

sentences.text: Therefore, his contention is not valid and not proved.

17. Further, the Respondent No.2 got examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 4 i.e.,
authorisation, discharge summary, copy of ESI bill and aadhar card.
In the cross examination he has admitted that Rs.82,275/- only has been reimbursed.
Further Respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Executive as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.5 and 6 i.e., authorisation letter and copy of policy.
During cross examination of RW.2, he admits that the charge sheet is filed against the insured driver.
He admits that there is no mention of No DL to the insured driver and the insured vehicle comes under lMV.
He also admits that the driver of the insured vehicle had valid driving licence for LMV and denied the other suggestions made by the learned advocate for petitioner.
18. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 argued that the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-ED-886 had no DL and he had not wore helmet.
But such things are not found in the charge sheet.
The police did not file charge sheet against the rider of the motor bike.
Moreover, the petitioner is pillion rider of the said motor vehicle.
Hence, contributory negligence cannot be attributed against the petitioner.

19. Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
20. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
21. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 42 years.
He has produced Aadhar card marked at ExP.9 to prove his age.
As per aadhar card, his date of birth is shown as 01.01.1978.
The accident has taken place on 17.10.2020.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 42 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.

22. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as driver and was earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove avocation and income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.14,500/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2020, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
23. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
24.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
25. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
26.

The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 20.10.2020 to 22-10-2020 at ESI hospital, Rajajinagar and he was admitted as an inpatient from 22.10.2020 to 30-10-2020 at Spine Care and Ortho Care hospital.

sentences.text: He was underwent surgery.
Further, P.W.3 Dr.K.Surendra Shetty has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 11 days.
27. Further, he might have taken atleast two months for recovery.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,000/- under this head (@ Rs.14,500/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
28.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
29. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.

In order to prove this fact, he has produced 16 Raju Alias Raja vs Ravishankar B.G on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82654548/

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/
COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

30. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he cannot stand for longer period, cannot walk without support of stick, cannot climb stairs, cannot squat on ground, cannot use Indian type of toilet, cannot sleep on right side, cannot move his right leg freely as before the accident.
31.
Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.K.Surendra Shetty as P.W.3 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, he got marked case sheet, X-rays and CD at Ex.P.17 to 19.
He assessed permanent disability of right lower limb at 60% and whole body disability at 30%.
32. In the cross-examination, PW.3 has admitted that after two years of discharge from the hospital he has assessed the disability.
He has admitted that fractures are united, shortening is there.
He has also admitted there is no infection.
He has also admitted that inpatient bill was claimed from ESI.
He has also admitted that he has personally operated and treated the petitioner.
33. Learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that the petitioner is professional driver, he can not do work as driver.
Hence the functional disability has to be taken higher side.

In this regard he relied the following judgments:
1.

In 2015 ACJ 721 between Jakir Hussain Vs. Sabir and others:
wherein it is held that the "insurer was professional driver and he suffered 55%
permanent disability and he cannot drive vehicle, therefore, 100% functional disability was taken."

34. But in the case on hand, though the petitioner claims that he is a professional driver but, he had not produced any evidence.
He has not deposed where he was working.
He has not examined his employer.
But simply says that he was working as driver.
In fact he has not produced his driving licence to show that he was the driver.
In his cross examination at one stretch he says that he has no DL, but in another stretch he says that his driving licence was misplaced at the time of accident.
In his statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. recorded before the police which is marked at Ex.P.2 he says that he was working as a coolie.
But in the petition he shows that he is the driver.
Hence, he failed to prove that he was the professional driver.
Hence, functional disability cannot be taken as prayed by him.
35. The Doctor has assessed permanent disability of right lower limb at 60% and whole body at 30%.

Upon careful consideration of the assessment of disability made by PW.3 keeping in mind the fact that PW.1 personally appeared before this court and deposed, also keeping in mind the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 and the treatment which he has taken, Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed appears to be at the higher rate.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 20% would be just and proper.
36. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 14.

With multiplier of 14, income of Rs.14,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 20%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.4,87,200/- (Rs.14,500/- x 12 x 14 x 20/100 =Rs.4,87,200/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,87,200/- under this head.

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.6,25,400/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
38.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-43-8593.
39.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 in his written arguments states that the driver of the offending car had licence to drive LMV and hence, he did not possess effective driving licence.
Admittedly, in the case on hand offending vehicle is the motor car used for commercial purpose.
The respondent No.1 had driving licence to drive the LMV motor vehicle.

In the judgments relied by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 Mukund Dewagan (Supra), The Managing Director, SBI (supra) and The Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd., (Supra), the Hon'ble Apex court and High Court of Karnataka held that driver possessed licence to drive LMV is competent to drive a transport vehicle where the gross weight /unladen weight of the vehicle does not exceed 7500 KG.

Therefore,
this Tribunal opines that driver of the offending vehicle had valid driving licence at the time of accident.

40. In the judgment relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner in the case of Venkataramanappa (Supra) it is held that ESI Act does not bar right to claim compensation against third parties though he was admitted in the ESI hospital and received reimbursement of medical expenses, he is entitled to claim compensation in the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the accident was not occurred during the course of employment, but admittedly, it is road traffic accident.

Therefore, though the petitioner has took treatment in the ESI hospital and received reimbursement of medical bills, as member of the ESI Corporation, it cannot be said that the claim petition filed under the MV Act is barred by the Employees State Insurance Act.

Even the petitioner is not claiming the medical bill amount of Rs.82,275/- which is reimbursed from ESI.
42.
There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car in question.
There is no dispute of the fact that the policy in respect of said vehicle was valid and effective as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
43. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.6,25,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,000/- under this head (@ Rs.14,500/- per month).
In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.11,200/- as a compensation under this head.
With multiplier of 14, income of Rs.14,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 20%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.4,87,200/- (Rs.14,500/- x 12 x 14 x 20/100 =Rs.4,87,200/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,87,200/- under this head.
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40.000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.
Medical expenses Rs. 11,200/-
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 29,000/-
laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.4,87,200/-
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
43. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.6,25,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
